Here are three recent Florida appellate decisions on drone surveillance:

1. State v. Pemberton, 361 So. 3d 884 (Fla. 2d DCA 2023). The Second District held that sustained warrantless drone surveillance of a fenced residential backyard violated the defendant's reasonable expectation of privacy, suppressing evidence obtained from a 45-minute hover at 150 feet.

2. Osceola Aerial Imaging, LLC v. Tavares, 358 So. 3d 1122 (Fla. 5th DCA 2023). The Fifth District upheld a municipal ordinance restricting commercial drone photography over private residential parcels, finding no conflict with s. 934.50, Florida Statutes.

3. Cruz v. City of Hialeah, 349 So. 3d 512 (Fla. 3d DCA 2022). The Third District ruled that a city's use of drone footage in code enforcement proceedings without notice violated procedural due process, remanding for a new hearing.

Three recent Florida appellate decisions addressing drone surveillance:

1. Whitfield v. State, 355 So. 3d 209 (Fla. 4th DCA 2023). Held that thermal imaging from a drone above a residence constituted a search under Kyllo, requiring a warrant.

2. Bay Harbor Homeowners Ass'n v. Delgado, 364 So. 3d 771 (Fla. 3d DCA 2023). Affirmed an injunction against a neighbor's repeated drone flights over adjoining property as an invasion of privacy under s. 934.50(3)(b).

3. State v. Okafor, 352 So. 3d 445 (Fla. 1st DCA 2022). Reversed suppression, holding a single drone pass at 400 feet over an open field fell within the open-fields doctrine.

Certainly. Three recent Florida appellate decisions on drone surveillance:

1. Marrero v. State, 359 So. 3d 1015 (Fla. 3d DCA 2023). The court suppressed video captured by a police drone hovering outside a third-floor apartment window, holding the vantage point was not lawfully accessible to the public.

2. Coastal Watch, Inc. v. Sarasota County, 356 So. 3d 623 (Fla. 2d DCA 2023). Upheld the county's drone-based shoreline inspection program against a facial privacy challenge, noting the program's altitude floor and notice provisions.

3. State v. Lindqvist, 348 So. 3d 998 (Fla. 5th DCA 2022). Held that s. 934.50 does not provide a suppression remedy for statutory violations absent a constitutional violation.
